While many investors have put their faith in the perpetual earnings growth of the so-called "Magnificent Seven" mega-cap stocks, Stephan Kemper, chief investment strategist at BNP Paribas Wealth Management, warns U.S. large cap equities are “extremely expensive”.

Following President Donald Trump securing a second term in office in November, Kemper’s team upgraded U.S. equities from neutral to overweight, with a preference for small and midcap equities. ... The earnings yield of the S&P 500 recently turned negative for the first time in decades, which he called "a clear warning sign.” ... “At least in the short-term, we expect Trump policies to be gross positive for US equities."
